scope: Paraphrased from Huang and Yang’s September 2026 preprint, Table 1 and Sections 2–4. These are the audit authors’ recovered records, not a new independent artifact audit. Assignment and filtering are separate questions; aligned evidence can still describe a selected population.
checklist: Record the exact release and the intended task.
Identify what produced the label, where it was observed and whether endpoint access was required.
State what the label means: application, user activity, server domain, visited site or maliciousness.
Trace the evidence unit to the released sample: aligned, inherited, derived or reused.
Record filtering, discarded samples and the population before selection; preserve lineage and evidence sources.

datasets.note: A capture’s activity label does not by itself prove the role of each contained flow.
Track inherited activity labels and reused source captures separately.
Application provenance and a downstream malicious/benign interpretation are distinct claims.
Endpoint-derived evidence may not be visible to a network observer.
SNI identifies a named server; this does not automatically establish the generating application. Account for SNI-based selection.

datasets.evidence: SNI in the audited released mapping
datasets.note: The audit distinguishes original browsing-run labels from connection-level mappings. It reports 41 classes/123,000 sessions in its artifact, versus the original paper’s 40/120,000; preserve release/version differences.
The audit could not confirm the public release form. The label provenance record remains incomplete.
